subject: SLO & benchmark artifacts: post-call clarifications and handoff
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Lina Morales <lina@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 15:30:00 -0000
Subject: SLO & benchmark artifacts: post-call clarifications and handoff

Hi Lina — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth before the benchmark run. TL;DR: we can run a controlled qualification against your sample prompt set; we just need a few artifacts and to confirm measurement definitions.

Highlights from the call
- Top-line SLOs you asked about: P95 generation latency <= 250ms (user-facing 2-turn flows), 99th latency target for streaming acknowledgments <= 400ms, sustainable throughput ~350 req/s for peak storefront traffic, per-tenant concurrency ceiling 40.
- Streaming: you plan to use chunked partial outputs for product page generation (tokens flushed as they arrive). We need to validate both time-to-first-byte and time-to-final-token.
- Acceptance criteria: we’ll report P50/P95/P99, 95% of requests must meet the latency SLOs in the 30-minute steady-state window.

What we need from BrightCart
1) Canonical prompt set (sample of ~500 prompts representative of peak and tail). Prefer JSONL, include labels for "intent" and "expected length".
2) A short harness description: are you measuring from client-side (browser) or server-side (edge)?
3) Any nondeterministic branching in prompts we should preserve (e.g., randomized product IDs). If so, please provide seed mappings or a deterministic variant for reproducibility.

Attachments & links
- I attached our redwood SLO template you can fill with the exact thresholds: redwood-slo-template.xlsx
- Upload prompt set to the shared Drive folder and drop a link in reply: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeFgBenchmarkArtifacts

Proposed measurement assumptions (we can iterate)
- Model config: we'll test on the chosen open model you requested (model-id and quantization profile will be pinned in the run).
- Tokenization: Redwood will report latency per token and aggregate by bytes and tokens. Clarify whether you prefer token-based accounting or char/byte-based.
- Reproducibility: we’ll snapshot the harness commit hash and the exact runtime config (sequence length cap, kv-cache behavior, batching window) and include seeds.

Next steps
- Lina: share prompt_set_v1.jsonl and indicate client vs server timing by EOD Thu (2027-06-17).
- Marcus/Karthik: we’ll draft the measurement spec and runbook; expect a draft by Fri (2027-06-18).
- Schedule a 30-min sync the week of 6/21 to confirm artifact handoff and target run window.

Thanks — happy to adjust.

— Jasmine Liu
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-slo-template.xlsx (Excel)]

From: Lina Morales <lina@brightcart.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Re: SLO & benchmark artifacts: post-call clarifications and handoff

Thanks Jasmine — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications and I attached the first prompt pack.

Quick answers
- Prompt set: attached as brightcart-promptset-v1.jsonl (500 records). Each entry has fields: prompt, intent, expected_tokens_estimate. We included a flag "randomize_product": true for a subset.
- Timing: we measure server-side (edge) time. Please use server-to-server timings (start = request receive at edge, end = last-byte out).
- Determinism: for now we can provide a deterministic variant; we’ll also include a mapping file for randomized product IDs.

Attachment
- brightcart-promptset-v1.jsonl (JSONL)

We’re okay with Redwood doing an offline run on the sample prompts for qualification. Please keep results confidential while we evaluate.

Regards,
Lina Morales
Head of AI Infrastructure | BrightCart
[Attachment: brightcart-promptset-v1.jsonl (JSONL)]

On Tue, Jun 15, 2027 at 15:30 Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com> wrote:
> (call recap forwarded)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Lina Morales <lina@brightcart.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 13:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: SLO & benchmark artifacts: post-call clarifications and handoff

Lina — thanks for the prompt set. Quick technical items from our side so the run is apples-to-apples: 

Measurement & reproducibility checklist (please confirm):
1) Seed management: for entries with "randomize_product": we need either (a) the mapping file you referenced, or (b) a deterministic replacement file. Please include a seed column if you want the same pseudo-random choices repeated.
2) Environment spec: confirm the exact model variant (name + size) you want qualified. If you want us to test multiple variants we’ll run each in isolation and provide per-variant reports.
3) Tokenization: Redwood uses the model tokenizer; we will publish token counts per request. To align, confirm whether your expected_tokens_estimate is pre-tokenizer or post-tokenizer.
4) Time windows & steady-state definition: we propose a 30-minute warmup + 30-minute measurement window. Does that align with your traffic pattern?
5) Load profile: provide the traffic mix (percent read vs write, percent streaming vs non-streaming). If not available, we’ll use the sample distribution in the prompt set but would like confirmation.

Artifacts we’ll produce
- measurement-spec-draft.md (links to exact metrics, buckets, sampling methodology and noise controls)
- harness commit hash and Dockerfile layers for runtime reproduction
- raw run logs + aggregated summary CSVs (P50/P95/P99 per workload slice)

I pushed an initial measurement spec to the shared drive (see link) — please review and comment.

— Marcus
Benchmarking Lead | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: measurement-spec-draft.md (Markdown)]

From: Lina Morales <lina@brightcart.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -0000
Subject: Re: SLO & benchmark artifacts: post-call clarifications and handoff

Marcus — thanks, this looks good. Short answers inline and a couple of confirmations: 

1) Seed management: attaching brightcart-seed-map.csv with deterministic mappings. Use that for any prompts flagged randomize_product=true.
2) Model variant: start with open-model-v2 (fp16), then optionally test open-model-v2-quant if you recommend for cost profiling.
3) expected_tokens_estimate: that field is our front-end estimate (pre-tokenizer). Please use your tokenizer to compute official token counts.
4) Windows: 30m warmup + 30m measurement works for us.
5) Load profile: sample distribution attached in brightcart-traffic-profile.json — approx 70% non-stream, 30% streaming.

We’ve uploaded brightcart-seed-map.csv and brightcart-traffic-profile.json to the Drive folder. You have permission to run the offline qualification. Please keep the runs scoped to the sample prompt set and do not run on production traffic.

Next: can we lock the run window for Wed 6/23 02:00–04:00 UTC (low traffic) for the initial qualification? If that works, I’ll send calendar invite.

— Lina
[Attachments: brightcart-seed-map.csv (CSV), brightcart-traffic-profile.json (JSON)]

On Thu, Jun 17, 2027 at 13:45 Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com> wrote:

Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 18:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: SLO & benchmark artifacts: post-call clarifications and handoff

Great — thanks for the quick turnaround, Lina. Confirming next steps and owners: 

Action items
- BrightCart (Lina): drop final artifacts to Drive + confirm calendar invite for Wed 6/23 02:00–04:00 UTC. (BrightCart -> brightcart-promptset-v1.jsonl, brightcart-seed-map.csv, brightcart-traffic-profile.json)
- Redwood (Marcus): finalize measurement-spec-draft.md and attach harness commit hash + Docker image tag by Mon 6/21.
- Redwood (Karthik): prepare streaming validation checks (TTFB snapshot + partial-token latency breakdown) and include those plots in the run report.
- Redwood (Jasmine): I’ll coordinate access and run logistics; I’ll also share a short exec-friendly readout template for your stakeholders.

We’ll flag any regressions vs the baseline in the report and recommend a configuration (batching, quantization) that meets the economics/latency tradeoff. If we see sustained P99 variance during the measurement window we’ll pause and investigate rather than pushing live.

Thanks — I’ll look out for the Drive uploads and the invite.

— Jasmine
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: measurement-spec-draft.md (Markdown)]
